question.prompt: If \(3x^3-9x^2+kx-12\) is divisible by \(x-3,\) then it is also divisible by:

solutions.explanation:
Let \(P(x)=3x^3-9x^2+kx-12\). If \(x-3\) divides \(P(x)\), then \(P(x)=(x-3)Q(x)\) for some polynomial \(Q\). Substituting \(x=3\) therefore gives \(P(3)=0\), which determines \(k\):
\[
0=3(3)^3-9(3)^2+3k-12
=3k-12.
\]
Hence \(k=4\). Now group the terms to reveal the known factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(x)&=3x^3-9x^2+4x-12\\
&=3x^2(x-3)+4(x-3)\\
&=(x-3)(3x^2+4).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the polynomial is also divisible by \(\boxed{3x^2+4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Find k, then factor
